title: Add support for AX.25 extended sequence number mode
description:
This is my first change to wireshark. I don't seem to have the right QT libraries, so I have only tested tshark. It works, but I don't know if I've done it the right way.

My test has been:

```
tshark -o ax25.extended:false -Vr mytest.pcap
tshark -o ax25.extended:true -Vr mytest.pcap
tshark -o ax25.extended:false -r mytest.pcap
tshark -o ax25.extended:true -r mytest.pcap
```

added 3 commits

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/17121/diffs?diff_id=1109461865&start_sha=806d9ff0d2dc040b00196fc9f64509c1cf67c1c5)
Hi Thomas, look good, can you share a pcap ?

Sure. Here's one with extended (mod128), and one with mod8.

* https://cement.retrofitta.se/tmp.hidden/ax25-ext.pcap
* https://cement.retrofitta.se/tmp.hidden/ax25-mod8.pcap

To get correct decoding, this means running:

```
tshark -Vr ax25-mod8.pcap # false looks like it's default in prefs API.
tshark -o ax25.extended:false -Vr ax25-mod8.pcap
tshark -o ax25.extended:true -Vr ax25-ext.pcap
```

Because the standard doesn't indicate extended or not, one has to guess.

The Linux implementation sets some reserved bits to indicate extended, but this PR doesn't look at that. A potential future PR could use it as a heuristic, but I'm not sure wireshark has heuristics.

It'd also be possible to infer the extendedness by seeing the SABM vs SABME, but I don't know how wireshark would do that. Also I wouldn't want to rely on it too much. AX.25 is not as robust as, say, TCP, and straggling packets could ruin everything.

Oh right, I can upload them here, too:

* [ax25-mod8.pcap](/uploads/a5b84f086e7a7c4b1d09ba137bb2b3b9/ax25-mod8.pcap)
* [ax25-ext.pcap](/uploads/d1e2f4703a83ee9206201d1d5fb4c6f8/ax25-ext.pcap)
